subject: Coaching T24: Khan Academy brand critique -- 5 points with MCM differentiation
body:
COACHING SUBMISSION T24: Competitor Brand Critique
Competitor: Khan Academy (khanacademy.org -- math, widely used, free, no login wall)
5-point critique with MCM differentiation case

---

POINT 1: Brand identity (where they are, where we are)
Khan Academy: seafoam green + teal (#1865F2 blue, #1DB954-adjacent), rounded corners, friendly cartoon mascots, learning badges. Brand says: "learning is approachable, everyone can do it."
MCM: Detroit Pistons palette, sharp edges, Grade 1-4 system, coach voice. Brand says: "you are preparing for a specific test, and you will be held to the standard."
Differentiation is CORRECT for Kai. Khan's brand removes stakes. MCM's brand installs them. Kai does not need encouragement that learning is accessible -- she knows the test is in 3 days.

POINT 2: Information density
Khan Academy: one question at a time, large font, heavy whitespace, hint button prominent, no timer visible.
MCM: all questions on one scroll, timer in header, submit at bottom.
Khan's approach is gentler on ADHD. One-question-at-a-time reduces the need to self-regulate scroll position. This is a place MCM should learn from. GD T18 spec (post-wrong micro-CTA) is a step toward this. But long-term, a one-question-per-page mode for exam.html would be a meaningful ADHD improvement.
Where MCM is correct: the all-on-one-page view lets Kai see the full scope of the test before starting, which reduces anxiety about unknowns. There's a valid tradeoff. Khan's approach sacrifices that overview.

POINT 3: Feedback timing
Khan Academy: immediate per-question feedback. Wrong answer shows explanation inline, hints are progressive (3 levels). No waiting.
MCM: feedback at end of exam (correct/incorrect border during exam, full explanation at grade).
Khan wins on ADHD reward timing. Their model matches the science in T17 (immediate feedback in the dopamine window). MCM's model is realistic to how tests work -- but for PRACTICE exams, per-question immediate feedback is the right call. Already partially implemented: answer border color changes immediately. The gap is the explanation text, which only appears post-grade.

POINT 4: Score communication
Khan Academy: mastery percentage by topic, animated progress ring, "Mastered" / "Familiar" / "Not yet started" labels.
MCM: Grade 1-4 with per-standard score breakdown in "Your Game Plan" section.
MCM's approach is more specific to Kai's actual test performance. SAAS grades on a 1-4 scale. Khan's mastery model is great for long-term skill building but the "Mastered" label can feel dishonest after one attempt. MCM's Grade 4 = you hit the standard on this attempt is more honest and more Kai-appropriate.

POINT 5: Visual hierarchy on results screen
Khan Academy: clean, whitespace-heavy, only 2-3 items on screen at a time.
MCM: scorecard stacks grade, coach message, AND standards grid in one scroll -- can feel like a lot.
Khan is correct here. The scorecard in MCM should show: grade (primary), coach message (secondary), and a separate disclosure to see the standards breakdown. Not all at once. GD should spec a scorecard redesign with progressive disclosure for the next GA sprint.
